# FMLA Eligibility Interpretation Memo — Bluestone
To: Megan Osei, HR Director
From: Rosa Coleman, Counsel
Date: 02/18/2026
Re: Brandon Lindqvist leave eligibility

## Question and governing rule
Bluestone Distribution asked whether Brandon Lindqvist may take job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) for a qualifying serious health condition. This memo addresses employee eligibility, not whether the reported condition qualifies or whether a particular absence is protected.

Under 29 U.S.C. § 2611(2), an employee generally must have worked for the employer for at least 12 months and at least 1,250 hours during the 12 months immediately before leave begins. The employee must also work at a site where the employer has at least 50 employees within 75 miles. For FMLA purposes, the hours test is 1,000 hours in the preceding 12 months.

## Records reviewed
| Item | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Hire date | 08/14/2024 |
| Requested leave start | 03/02/2026 |
| Hours worked, 03/02/2025–03/01/2026 | 1,260 |
| Employees within 75 miles of Brandon's worksite | 53 |
| Employer size | At least 68 employees for 20 workweeks in 2025 |

## Application and recommendation
Brandon has been employed for more than 12 months by the requested leave date, and the recorded 1,260 hours exceed the applicable hours threshold. Bluestone also meets the employer coverage requirement, and the worksite count exceeds 50 within 75 miles.

Despite that headcount, Brandon is not eligible because the worksite has fewer than 50 employees within 75 miles. HR should therefore deny FMLA protection on eligibility grounds, while separately reviewing any applicable state or local leave rights and the company's leave policy. Do not characterize this memo as a determination that the medical condition is or is not FMLA-qualifying.

errors.explanation: The memo gives the wrong FMLA hours threshold. The governing rule stated just above it is 1,250 hours worked during the 12 months before leave begins, which is the federal eligibility standard.
errors.fix: the hours test is 1,250 hours in the preceding 12 months

errors.quote: Brandon is not eligible because the worksite has fewer than 50 employees within 75 miles
errors.explanation: The records table shows 53 employees within 75 miles of Brandon’s worksite, so the stated reason for finding him ineligible contradicts the memo’s own data. The application section also notes that the worksite count exceeds 50.
errors.fix: Brandon is eligible because the worksite has at least 50 employees within 75 miles
